data.title: Small details, better interfaces
data.excerpt: A few practical habits for making everyday interfaces feel considered.
data.bodyMarkdown:
An interface is made of small decisions. A label, a loading state, and a little extra breathing room can change how a product feels.

This is sample writing for the portfolio. It demonstrates the reading experience; it is not a record of a published article.

## Start with the next action

Before adding another component, ask what someone is trying to do on this screen. Put that action where they can find it, and describe it with a familiar verb.

A good button label can often replace a paragraph of instructions.

## Make states part of the design

A list does not always contain data. It can be loading, empty, unavailable, or complete. Each state needs a useful response.

| State | What the interface should do |
| --- | --- |
| Loading | Keep the layout steady and explain what is happening |
| Empty | Explain what will appear here |
| Error | Offer a clear way to try again |
| Success | Show the result without unnecessary ceremony |

## Leave room to read

Keep lines comfortable, use a small set of type sizes, and let spacing communicate relationships. A heading should belong to the paragraph beneath it.

> The details work best when they help someone move forward.

The goal is a product that feels easy to understand, even when the work behind it is complex.
